Answer: B
Reason: The chest X-ray demonstrates radiolucent streaks of air outlining the mediastinal structures (pneumomediastinum), which, combined with the history of an alcoholic binge (suggesting vomiting/retching) and neck swelling, is most consistent with spontaneous pneumomediastinum or early Boerhaave syndrome caused by alveolar rupture or esophageal injury. Among the choices, identifying pneumomediastinum is the accurate radiographic finding.
